title: Relative logarithmic differential symbol sheaf on arbitrary schemes
statement: Let $X,Y$ be arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme] with etale log structures $M,N$ and log morphism $f:(X,M)\to(Y,N)$ as in [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation]. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $R_X$ be the structure ring sheaf $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$, regarded as a sheaf of rings by forgetting commutativity. The symbol presheaf has sections $\mathcal O_X(U)\sqcup M(U)$, with the original restrictions. Form its free $R_X$-module presheaf, with symbols $da$ and $d\log m$. Let $K_f$ be the least presheaf submodule containing, on every test object, the relations $d(a+b)-da-db$, $d(ab)-a\,db-b\,da$, $d\log(mm\prime)-d\log m-d\log m\prime$, $d\alpha(m)-\alpha(m)d\log m$, and the symbols $d(k^\sharp b)$ and $d\log(f^\flat n)$ for every compatible relative etale diagram $V\to U$ over $f$, with $b\in\mathcal O_Y(U)$ and $n\in N(U)$. Define the differential presheaf to be the cokernel of $K_f\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Free}(\mathcal O_X\sqcup M)$ in module presheaves. Define $\omega_f$ as its module sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], a sheaf of $R_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The generator map is the free-module quotient map followed by the sheafification unit; its values on the two symbols define $d$ and $d\log$ as actual sections of $\omega_f$. These constructions require neither fineness, saturation, log smoothness nor Noetherianness.
